fact: La Nation reports that the tripartite agreement signed in Djibouti on 4 February 2026 by Djibouti Telecom, Ethio telecom and Sudatel covers construction and maintenance of a cross-border terrestrial fibre link joining Djibouti, Ethiopia and Sudan.

La Nation reports on 2026-09-09 that the three operators presented Horizon to hyperscalers and carriers in Addis Ababa on 2026-09-07, in a pre-commercialisation phase before deployment and commercial launch, describing it as a future infrastructure.

Ethio telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel Group converted their December 2024 memorandum into a binding agreement on the Horizon Fiber cross-border terrestrial corridor from Djibouti through Ethiopia to Sudan; the document gives no signing day, so the published date is used.

The three operators signed a binding tripartite agreement to operationalise Horizon Fiber, a terrestrial fibre corridor from Djibouti's submarine cable gateways through Ethiopia to Sudan, signed at a ceremony in Djibouti; the document gives no day, so the published date is used.

Ethio Telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel turned a December 2024 cross-border fibre memorandum into a binding agreement for a terrestrial corridor from Djibouti's landing stations through Ethiopia to Sudan's landing stations; the document gives no signing day, so the published date is used.

La Nation reports that the three operators signed on Wednesday 4 February 2026 in Djibouti the agreement to launch Horizon, a planned terrestrial corridor of about 2,800 km with 144 fibre pairs joining Djibouti, Addis Ababa and Port Sudan, following a memorandum signed in Addis Ababa on 4 December 2024.

Ethio telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel signed a tripartite contractual agreement in Djibouti to implement Horizon Fiber, a cross-border fibre corridor from Djibouti's landing stations through Ethiopia into Sudan, per TechAfrica News.
